solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Horse flying past us has no time to circulate for example

indicators.note: to circulate is to go around, so the outer letters ring the abbreviation
having no time means the letter for time, T, is dropped from the word

parts.note: taken as written before the deletion
taken as written

explanation.surface: A horse races past us at a gallop, too hurried to mingle with the crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Horse flying' is the definition; 'has no time' leaves PAS, and 'to circulate' wraps PASUS round the example abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: The winged steed of Greek myth is the classic flying horse.

clue.text: Risky fusion of rap and soul

indicators.note: a fusion melts things together into a new mixture, so the letters of both words are blended and rearranged

explanation.surface: A music critic dismisses a rap-soul crossover as a dangerous experiment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fusion of' mixes RAP and SOUL, seven letters, into the answer; 'and' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Parlous is an old-fashioned word for dangerous or precarious, a synonym of risky.

clue.text: Party earlier held by private secretary somewhere in the Pacific

parts.note: a gala is a festive party or celebration

indicators.note: being held by something means sitting inside it, so the other pieces go within the outer letters

parts.note: PS is the standard abbreviation for private secretary
ago means in the past, earlier than now

explanation.surface: An office assistant hosts a party in advance of a trip to a Pacific destination.
explanation.definitionFit: The Galapagos Islands are an archipelago in the eastern Pacific, so they are an example of a place there.

clue.text: Harris's neighbour beginning to retrieve powerful cricket shot?

parts.note: Skye is the Hebridean island lying next to Harris off western Scotland

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, so only the opening letter is taken

explanation.surface: A Hebridean islander's neighbour starts fetching a ball after a big hit.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a skyer is a ball hit very high into the air; the question mark marks this as a description by example.
explanation.definitionFit: A skyer is a mighty hit that sends the cricket ball high into the sky, a type of shot.

clue.text: Burial site not promoted in south — terribly old

indicators.note: one piece sitting in another means it is placed inside it
terribly suggests something badly mangled, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder

indicators.note: in a down clue, promoted means moved upwards, so the word is read from bottom to top

explanation.surface: Someone passed over for promotion in the South grumbles that it is all terribly antiquated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terribly' gives SUTHOO; 'promoted' (upwards in a down light) gives TON, set 'in' it. Sutton Hoo is in Suffolk, eastern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Sutton Hoo in Suffolk is the famous Anglo-Saxon ship burial ground, so it is an example of a burial site.

clue.text: Observer section features special wine

indicators.note: something that features an item contains it, so the letter goes inside the longer word

parts.note: the retina is the light-sensitive section of the eye, the organ an observer uses

explanation.surface: A section of a Sunday newspaper runs a feature on a notable wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Observer' looks like the British Sunday newspaper, but it means a looker, whose eye has a retina.
explanation.definitionFit: Retsina is a Greek white wine flavoured with pine resin.

clue.text: Female is surfacing among eggs

indicators.note: being among things means sitting inside them, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: roe is a mass of fish eggs

indicators.note: in a down clue, surfacing means rising upwards, so the word is read from bottom to top

explanation.surface: A female fish rises to the surface among a mass of eggs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surfacing' turns IS to SI, which goes 'among' ROE.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosie is a woman's name, so a female is defined by example in crossword fashion.

clue.text: Lad's weary, revising fictional character

parts.note: Tom is a typical lad's name, and the possessive adds the S

indicators.note: revising a text means reworking it, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A boy is tired out from revising for exams.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lad's' supplies a boy's name with possessive S; 'revising' looks like exam study but signals the rearrangement to SAWYER.
explanation.definitionFit: Tom Sawyer is Mark Twain's boy hero, a famous character in fiction.

clue.text: Spotted horse, lacking power, weak, getting carried along

indicators.note: lacking something means being without it, so that letter is removed from the word

parts.note: a pinto is a horse with patchy, piebald markings
P is the abbreviation for power in physics

explanation.surface: A dappled horse with no strength left, feeble, is being towed along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking' removes P from PINTO, leaving INTO.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in tow is being pulled behind, carried along by another vehicle.

clue.text: Stuck present in hands of tot

indicators.note: something in the hands of another is held inside its grip, so the word goes within the outer letters

parts.note: to tot up is to add
here means present, as when answering a register

explanation.surface: A gift held by a toddler got stuck to its fingers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tot' looks like a small child but is the verb meaning sum up, ADD.
explanation.definitionFit: Adhered is a synonym of stuck, as in clung firmly to a surface.

clue.text: Team of workers again put down path?

definitions.meaning: a shift or crew of workers who take over from another
to put down a path once more is to lay it a second time

explanation.definitionFit: A relay is a team taking turns at a job; re-lay is to lay again, as with paving.

clue.text: Tenor in France is lighter, sporting tie

parts.note: T is an abbreviation for tenor in music
est is the French word for 'is'
a match is a small device for lighting fires

explanation.surface: A French singer lights up while wearing a sporty necktie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tie' is a match between two teams, not neckwear.
explanation.definitionFit: A test match is an international cricket or rugby fixture, a type of sporting contest.

clue.text: Deliberately, one holds back consommé to hide price

indicators.note: something that holds another contains it, so the rest go inside these letters

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: to hide something is to cover it from view, so the abbreviation goes inside
back means turned the other way, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: consommé is a clear soup
RP is short for retail price

explanation.surface: A diner returns a clear soup, intent on concealing the cost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' gives PUOS; 'to hide' and 'holds' nest the pieces as PURPOS inside the outer word.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something on purpose is doing it intentionally, a synonym phrase for deliberately.

clue.text: Unprepared army's rejected in conflict

indicators.note: rejected suggests thrown back, so the whole run of letters is read backwards

parts.note: raw means not ready or unprepared, like an untrained recruit
TA is the Territorial Army, with the 's standing for 'is'

explanation.surface: An ill-prepared army is turned away while fighting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns the whole of RAWTA backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Being at war means being engaged in armed conflict.

clue.text: Greek character's overlooking Troy, a symbol of disgrace

indicators.note: overlooking means missing out or ignoring, so the letter is left out

parts.note: a stigma is a mark of shame
t is the abbreviation for troy, the system of weights

explanation.surface: A Greek hero gazes down on Troy, a sign of its shame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Troy' looks like the ancient city but stands for troy weight, abbreviated T.
explanation.definitionFit: Sigma is the eighteenth letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Hair colouring on bed has ruined covers close to wall

indicators.note: something that covers another wraps round it, so the letter goes inside
ruined means wrecked, so these letters are jumbled into a new order
the close of a word is its end, so only its final letter is used

explanation.surface: A hair dye spilt on the bed has spoiled the covers right by the wall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruined' scrambles ONBEDHAS; 'covers' puts it round L, the 'close to' wall.
explanation.definitionFit: Ash blonde is a pale, greyish blond shade of hair.

clue.text: US industrialist sees bird crossing on track

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece on another follows it

parts.note: a hen is a female bird
RY is an abbreviation for railway, a track
a ford is a shallow place to cross a river

explanation.surface: An American tycoon spots a bird crossing the railway line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' means placed after in an across light; 'sees' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry Ford founded the Ford Motor Company and pioneered mass production of cars in America.

clue.text: Type of tenant perhaps Ginny strangely keeps on every year

indicators.note: something that keeps another holds it inside, so these pieces go within
strangely suggests oddly altered, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
PA stands for per annum, Latin for each year

explanation.surface: A landlady, Ginny, oddly lets her lodger stay on year after year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strangely' rearranges GINNY into NYING, and that 'keeps' ONPA after the first N.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenant who pays no rent is non-paying, an adjective describing such a kind of occupant.

clue.text: Precisely at that time, seaman catches sole? Just the opposite

indicators.note: something that catches another holds it inside
this reverses the stated roles, so the catcher becomes the one caught and vice versa

parts.note: sole means single, only one
then means at that time
OS is an ordinary seaman

explanation.surface: A sailor lands a flatfish just in time, or so it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: As written the seaman would catch the sole; 'Just the opposite' flips who contains whom. 'sole' looks like the fish but means single.
explanation.definitionFit: On the nose is an idiom meaning exactly or precisely, as in arriving on the nose.

clue.text: Wrongly cast woman ignores a shirt that's improper

indicators.note: improper means not as it should be, so the letters are rearranged
ignoring something leaves it out, so the letter is dropped

explanation.surface: A woman refuses to wear a shirt she considers unsuitable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignores' drops A from WOMAN, leaving WOMN; 'that's improper' mixes WOMN and SHIRT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something misthrown has been thrown badly, and cast is a synonym of thrown.

clue.text: Mike, soaked in shower, copes

parts.note: Mike is the NATO alphabet code word for M

indicators.note: a shower scatters things about, so the letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: Mike, drenched under the shower, manages as best he can.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in shower' gives AKESDO; 'soaked in shower' paints a wet scene, hiding the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To make do is an idiom for getting by with what is available, managing.

clue.text: Short water vole, literally

definitions.meaning: in The Wind in the Willows the character called the Water Rat is really a water vole

explanation.walkthrough: Ratty is the riverbank friend of Mole in Kenneth Grahame's children's book The Wind in the Willows.
explanation.definitionFit: Ratty means irritable or short-tempered, and it is also the name of Grahame's water-vole character.

clue.text: Reader will broadcast record that's a sign of Xmas

indicators.note: something broadcast is heard rather than seen, so the words are said aloud

parts.note: the reader is 'you', so 'reader will' is 'you'll'
a log is a written record

explanation.surface: A newsreader will announce a record-breaking Christmas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reader' means you, the person reading the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A Yule log, either a large log or a chocolate cake, is a traditional emblem of Christmas.

clue.text: Joint deficient before fifties? It's a sign of trouble

indicators.note: deficient means falling short, so the last letter is cut off

parts.note: the knee is a joint of the leg
L is the Roman numeral for fifty, so two of them make fifties

explanation.surface: A dodgy knee before someone hits fifty is a warning of problems ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deficient' cuts the last letter, leaving KNE; 'before' is only a link since the order already matches.
explanation.definitionFit: A knell is the tolling of a bell for a death, so figuratively an omen of disaster.

clue.text: Love god encapsulates universal currency

indicators.note: to encapsulate is to enclose in a capsule, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: Eros is the Greek god of love
U is the film classification for universal

explanation.surface: Cupid's Greek counterpart embodies a single global money.
explanation.definitionFit: Euros are the money units of the eurozone, so they are a currency.

clue.text: Intended to help male worker in Surrey town

indicators.note: one piece in another sits inside it

parts.note: Ewell is a town in Surrey, a county south of London
an ant is a typical worker insect in crosswords

explanation.surface: A man labours in a commuter town south of London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' gives EANTWELL; Ewell is a small town in Surrey, a county just south of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who meant well had good intentions, wanting to help even if it went wrong.

clue.text: Pupil lies in this bunk?

definitions.meaning: the pupil, the dark centre of the iris, sits in a person's own eye
bunk means nonsense, and '...!' is an exclamation of disbelief

explanation.definitionFit: My eye is a dated exclamation meaning nonsense; literally, a pupil lies within one's eye.

clue.text: Giant wings of insect occupy shade

indicators.note: to occupy a place is to be inside it, so the letters go within

parts.note: tan is a shade of brown

indicators.note: the wings of a word are its outer letters, first and last

explanation.surface: An insect's wings spread across a patch of shadow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wings of' takes IT from insect.
explanation.definitionFit: The Titans were giant deities of Greek myth, so titan means a giant.

clue.text: Plain green models shown in class one

indicators.note: shown in another word means placed inside it

parts.note: a set is a class or group, as in a school set

indicators.note: to model is to shape, so these letters are reshaped

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Simple green fashion is shown off in the first form at school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'models' gives RENGE and 'shown in' places it in the class word; the Serengeti is in Tanzania.
explanation.definitionFit: The Serengeti is a vast plain in Tanzania, so it is an example of a plain.

clue.text: Dwarfish creature right to be in charge

indicators.note: to be in something means sitting inside it

parts.note: a toll is a charge for using a road or bridge

explanation.surface: A small being thinks it has every right to take control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charge' looks like being in command but means a fee.
explanation.definitionFit: Trolls of Scandinavian folklore are sometimes small, dwarflike beings.

clue.text: Blue flower in Asia reportedly discovered

parts.note: the Ob is a great river in Siberia; a flower is something that flows

indicators.note: reportedly means as told, so the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: seen means spotted or discovered

explanation.surface: A blue bloom is said to have been found in Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' means a thing that flows, a river, not a bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue is used of jokes or films that are indecent, a sense shared with obscene.

clue.text: Horse, around 9, excitedly eats piece of sugar and root

indicators.note: being around something means surrounding it

parts.note: gee-gee, GG, is a childish word for horse

indicators.note: eating something takes it inside
excitedly suggests stirred up, so the letters are mixed

parts.note: the numeral 9 written as a word

indicators.note: a piece of the word here is its first letter

explanation.surface: A horse, about nine, eagerly munches a sugar lump and a root.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eats' and 'excitedly' make INSEN from the number and the sugar's S; 'around' sets the horse letters about it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ginseng is a medicinal plant root used in herbal remedies.
